e-8799.problem: The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots $x_1=x_2=2,x_3=1,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $3.$ Find $P(x).$
e-8799.worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${\color{black}x_1=x_2=2}$ and ${\color{black}x_3=1},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is ${\color{black}a=3},$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =3(x-2)(x-2)(x-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}3(x-2)(x-2)(x-1) & =3({x}^{2}-4x+4)(x-1) \\  & =3({x}^{3}-{x}^{2}-4{x}^{2}+4x+4x-4) \\  & =3({x}^{3}-5{x}^{2}+8x-4) \\  & =3{x}^{3}-15{x}^{2}+24x-12.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x) = 3x^3 -15x^2+24x-12.$

The Argand diagram above shows the roots of the cubic polynomial $f(x).$ Find $f(x)$ given that the coefficient of the cubic term is $1.$
e-5792.worked_solution:
From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${\color{black}x_1= 2}$ and ${\color{black}x_{2,3}=-2\pm \textrm{i}}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the cubic term is ${\color{black}a=1}.$ 

Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =(x-2)(x-(-2+\text{i}))(x-(-2-\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-2)(x-(-2+\text{i}))(x-(-2-\text{i})) & = \\ (x-2)({x}^{2}-x(-2-\text{i})-x(-2+\text{i})+(-2+\text{i})(-2-\text{i})) & = \\ (x-2)({x}^{2}+4x+5) & = \\ {x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}+5x-2{x}^{2}-8x-10 & = \\ {x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}-3x-10 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x) = x^3+2x^2-3x-10.$

decision.explanation: The repeated root -1 gives (x+1)^2, and the root 3 gives (x-3). With leading coefficient 2, P(x)=2(x+1)^2(x-3)=2(x^3-x^2-5x-3)=2x^3-2x^2-10x-6.

$$

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x+1)(x+1)(x-3) & =2({x}^{2}+2x+1)(x-3) \\  & =2({x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}+2{x}^{2}-6x+x-3) \\  & =2({x}^{3}-{x}^{2}-5x-3) \\  & =2{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-10x-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=2{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-10x-6.$

The cubic polynomial P(x) has roots x1=x2=−1,x3=3, and the coefficient of the cubic term is 2. Find P(x).

a
2x3+6x2−10x−6
b
2x3−x2−5x−3
c
2x3−6x2−2x+6
d
2x3+3x2−5x−3
e
2x3−2x2−10x−6
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since our cubic polynomial has roots x1=x2=−1 and x3=3, and the coefficient of the cubic term is a=2, we can write the polynomial as follows:

a(x−x1)(x−x2)(x−x3)=2(x−(−1))(x−(−1))(x−3)=2(x+1)(x+1)(x−3)

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

2(x+1)(x+1)(x−3)=2(x2+2x+1)(x−3)=2(x3−3x2+2x2−6x+x−3)=2(x3−x2−5x−3)=2x3−2x2−10x−6.

Therefore, P(x)=2x3−2x2−10x−6.

content.knowledge_point: Finding a Cubic Polynomial Given Three Real Roots and a Leading Coefficient
content.problem: The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=-1,{x}_{3}=3,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $2.$ Find $P(x).$
content.worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}={x}_{2}=-1$ and ${x}_{3}=3,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =2(x-(-1))(x-(-1))(x-3) \\  & =2(x+1)(x+1)(x-3)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x+1)(x+1)(x-3) & =2({x}^{2}+2x+1)(x-3) \\  & =2({x}^{3}-3{x}^{2}+2{x}^{2}-6x+x-3) \\  & =2({x}^{3}-{x}^{2}-5x-3) \\  & =2{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-10x-6.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=2{x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-10x-6.$

content.problem: The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-5,$ ${x}_{2}=0,$ and ${x}_{3}=1,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $-2.$ Find $P(x).$
content.worked_solution:
Since our cubic polynomial has roots ${x}_{1}=-5,$ ${x}_{1}=0,$ and ${x}_{3}=1,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=-2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =-2(x-(-5))(x-0)(x-1) \\  & =-2x(x+5)(x-1)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-2x(x+5)(x-1) & =-2x({x}^{2}+4x-5) \\  & =-2({x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}-5x) \\  & =-2{x}^{3}-8{x}^{2}+10x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=-2{x}^{3}-8{x}^{2}+10x.$

$$

The cubic polynomial P(x) has roots x1=−3, x2=0, and x3=5, and the coefficient of the cubic term is 2. Find P(x).

a
2x3−4x2−30x
b
2x3−2x2−30
c
2x3+4x2+15x
d
2x3+8x2+60x
e
2x3−4x−15
Submit

decision.explanation: The roots and leading coefficient give P(x)=2x(x+3)(x-5). Since (x+3)(x-5)=x^2-2x-15, P(x)=2x^3-4x^2-30x.

after.name: Question 4
after.problem: The cubic polynomial $P(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-3,$ ${x}_{2}=0,$ and ${x}_{3}=5,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $2.$ Find $P(x).$
after.worked_solution:
Since our cubic equation has roots ${x}_{1}=-3,$ ${x}_{2}=0,$ and ${x}_{3}=5,$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) & =2(x-(-3))(x-0)(x-5) \\  & =2x(x+3)(x-5)\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2x(x+3)(x-5) & =2x({x}^{2}-2x-15) \\  & =2({x}^{3}-2{x}^{2}-15x) \\  & =2{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}-30x.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $P(x)=2{x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}-30x.$

after.worked_solution:
Since $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-2$ and ${x}_{2,3}=3\pm \text{i},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=-1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =-1(x-(-2))(x-(3+\text{i}))(x-(3-\text{i})) \\  & =-(x+2)(x-(3+\text{i}))(x-(3-\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-(x+2)(x-(3+\text{i}))(x-(3-\text{i})) & = \\ -(x+2)({x}^{2}-x(3-\text{i})-x(3+\text{i})+(3+\text{i})(3-\text{i})) & = \\ -(x+2)({x}^{2}-6x+10) & = \\ -({x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}+10x+2{x}^{2}-12x+20) & = \\ -{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}+2x-20 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=-{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}+2x-20.$

The cubic polynomial f(x) has roots x1=−2,x2,3=3±i, and the coefficient of the cubic term is −1. Find f(x).

a
−x3+2x2−4x+10
b
−x3+4x2+2x−20
c
−x3+4x2+2x+20
d
x3−2x2+4x−10
e
x3−4x2−2x+20
Submit
Correct
EXPLANATION

Since f(x) has roots x1=−2 and x2,3=3±i, and the coefficient of the cubic term is a=−1, we can write the polynomial as follows:

f(x)=a(x−x1)(x−x2)(x−x3)=−1(x−(−2))(x−(3+i))(x−(3−i))=−(x+2)(x−(3+i))(x−(3−i))

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

−(x+2)(x−(3+i))(x−(3−i))=−(x+2)(x2−x(3−i)−x(3+i)+(3+i)(3−i))=−(x+2)(x2−6x+10)=−(x3−6x2+10x+2x2−12x+20)=−x3+4x2+2x−20.

Therefore, f(x)=−x3+4x2+2x−20.

content.problem: The cubic polynomial $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-2,{x}_{2,3}=3\pm \text{i},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $-1.$ Find $f(x).$
content.worked_solution:
Since $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-2$ and ${x}_{2,3}=3\pm \text{i},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=-1,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =-1(x-(-2))(x-(3+\text{i}))(x-(3-\text{i})) \\  & =-(x+2)(x-(3+\text{i}))(x-(3-\text{i}))\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}-(x+2)(x-(3+\text{i}))(x-(3-\text{i})) & = \\ -(x+2)({x}^{2}-x(3-\text{i})-x(3+\text{i})+(3+\text{i})(3-\text{i})) & = \\ -(x+2)({x}^{2}-6x+10) & = \\ -({x}^{3}-6{x}^{2}+10x+2{x}^{2}-12x+20) & = \\ -{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}+2x-20 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=-{x}^{3}+4{x}^{2}+2x-20.$

after.problem: The cubic polynomial $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-1,{x}_{2,3}=\pm 4\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $2.$ Find $f(x).$
after.worked_solution:
Since $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2,3}=\pm 4\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =2(x-(-1))(x-4\text{i})(x-(-4\text{i})) \\  & =2(x+1)(x-4\text{i})(x+4\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x+1)(x-4\text{i})(x+4\text{i}) & = \\ 2(x+1)({x}^{2}-(4\text{i})^{2}) & = \\ 2(x+1)({x}^{2}+16) & = \\ 2({x}^{3}+{x}^{2}+16x+16) & = \\ 2{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+32x+32 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=2{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+32x+32.$

Since $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=-1$ and ${x}_{2,3}=\pm 4\text{i},$ and the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=2,$ we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =2(x-(-1))(x-4\text{i})(x-(-4\text{i})) \\  & =2(x+1)(x-4\text{i})(x+4\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}2(x+1)(x-4\text{i})(x+4\text{i}) & = \\ 2(x+1)({x}^{2}-(4\text{i})^{2}) & = \\ 2(x+1)({x}^{2}+16) & = \\ 2({x}^{3}+{x}^{2}+16x+16) & = \\ 2{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+32x+32 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)=2{x}^{3}+2{x}^{2}+32x+32.$

From the diagram, we see that $f(x)$ has roots ${x}_{1}=4$ and ${x}_{2,3}=\pm 3\text{i}.$ Additionally, we're given that the coefficient of the cubic term is $a=1.$ Therefore, we can write the polynomial as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}f(x) & =a(x-{x}_{1})(x-{x}_{2})(x-{x}_{3}) \\  & =1(x-4)(x-3\text{i})(x-(-3\text{i})) \\  & =(x-4)(x-3\text{i})(x+3\text{i})\end{aligned}
$$

Expanding the parentheses, we obtain

$$
\begin{aligned}(x-4)(x-3\text{i})(x+3\text{i}) & = \\ (x-4)({x}^{2}-x(-3\text{i})-x(3\text{i})+(3\text{i})(-3\text{i})) & = \\ (x-4)({x}^{2}+9) & = \\ {x}^{3}+9x-4{x}^{2}-36 & = \\ {x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}+9x-36 & .\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, $f(x)={x}^{3}-4{x}^{2}+9x-36.$
